Kitchen Cabinet Quotation Malaysia: Sample & Price per Foot Run

Published 19 November 2026

A good kitchen cabinet quotation in Malaysia prices base, wall and tall cabinets separately, per foot run, and spells out the carcass board, door finish, hardware and countertop on every line. In 2026, published rates run roughly RM180–300 per foot run for melamine, RM330–600 for plywood and RM400–700 for aluminium. Below are the rates, how to measure, what to specify, and a sample quotation you can follow.

Kitchen cabinet price per foot run (2026)

Cabinet material Typical 2026 price per foot run Notes
Melamine on particle board RM180–300 Budget option, best for dry kitchens
Laminate (HPL) doors RM280–420 More scratch and heat resistant than melamine
Plywood carcass RM330–600 Holds screws and hinges better; common for wet kitchens
Aluminium RM400–700 Waterproof and termite-proof; premium ranges cost more
Tall cabinets (any material) about RM450–690 Priced higher per foot than base or wall units
Quartz countertop from about RM150–180 Priced per foot run of countertop

Upgrading to premium hinges and drawer runners adds roughly RM30–80 per foot run. A typical custom set of 15–20 feet of cabinets lands around RM4,500–12,000 installed, depending on material, before countertop and appliances.

These are published market ranges, not a price list. Your own rates depend on your supplier, factory and location.

How to measure a foot run

A foot run is one foot of cabinet length measured along the wall. It isn’t an area, so the cabinet’s height and depth are built into the rate.

  • Measure base, wall and tall cabinets separately. They have different rates, and a quotation that combines them can’t be checked or compared.
  • Say how you count corners. In an L-shaped kitchen, the corner can be counted in one run or both. Either is fine if it’s written down. Unexplained corner charges are a common reason clients distrust cabinet quotes.
  • Leave out gaps. The space for a freestanding fridge or a cooker hood without a cabinet isn’t a foot run of cabinet.
  • Re-measure on site before fabrication. Quote from the drawing, then confirm the final lengths on site, and price any difference at your quoted rate.

What to specify on each line

Clients compare quotes line by line, and the cheapest quote often has the vaguest description. Spell out:

  • Carcass board: melamine particle board, MDF, plywood or aluminium, and its thickness.
  • Door finish: melamine, laminate (HPL), acrylic, spray paint or aluminium.
  • Hardware: the hinge and drawer runner brand, and whether they’re soft-close.
  • Countertop: material, length and edge.
  • Cut-outs: sink, hob and any socket openings.
  • Plinth, end panels and fillers, if you charge for them separately.
  • Dismantling and disposal of the old kitchen.
  • Installation and delivery: included or charged separately.

Sample kitchen cabinet quotation

A 12-foot kitchen with base and wall cabinets, a tall cabinet for the oven, and a quartz countertop. The rates are illustrative, picked from within the published ranges above.

Item Unit Qty Rate (RM) Amount (RM)
Base cabinets, 18mm plywood carcass, laminate doors ft run 12 380.00 4,560.00
Wall cabinets, 18mm plywood carcass, laminate doors ft run 10 330.00 3,300.00
Tall cabinet, oven & microwave housing ft run 2 600.00 1,200.00
Quartz countertop ft run 12 200.00 2,400.00
Cut-outs for sink and hob nos 2 100.00 200.00
Soft-close hinges & drawer runners upgrade ft run 12 50.00 600.00
Dismantle & dispose existing cabinets lot 1 500.00 500.00
Total 12,760.00

Excluded: sink, tap, hob, cooker hood and other appliances; plumbing and electrical points; wall tiles and backsplash. Listing these stops the “I thought the hood was included” conversation at handover.

The wall run is two feet shorter than the base run because the cooker hood sits above the hob without a cabinet.

Common kitchen cabinet quotation mistakes

  • One lump sum for “kitchen cabinet”. The client can’t compare it, and you can’t price a change fairly.
  • No material spec. “Cabinet” could mean melamine or plywood, a difference of hundreds of ringgit per foot.
  • Combining base and wall cabinets into one rate, which hides how the price was worked out.
  • Forgetting dismantling, cut-outs or end panels, small lines that add up to real margin.
  • No validity date, so a client returns months later expecting the old board prices.

If the client changes the layout or upgrades the doors after approving the quote, put it in a variation order before you order materials.

Frequently asked questions

How much is a kitchen cabinet per foot run in Malaysia in 2026?
Published 2026 guides put melamine cabinets at roughly RM180 to RM300 per foot run, plywood at roughly RM330 to RM600, and aluminium at roughly RM400 to RM700. Tall cabinets cost more per foot than base or wall cabinets, and premium hardware adds to the rate.
How do you measure a foot run for kitchen cabinets?
Measure the length of the cabinets along the wall, in feet. Base cabinets, wall cabinets and tall cabinets are usually measured and priced separately. State in the quotation how corners are counted, so the client can compare quotes fairly.
What should a kitchen cabinet quotation include?
The length and rate for base, wall and tall cabinets separately; the carcass board, door finish and thickness; the hardware brand for hinges and drawer runners; the countertop material and length; cut-outs; dismantling of the old kitchen; and a clear list of what is excluded, such as appliances, sink, tap, plumbing and electrical points.
Which cabinet material is best for a wet kitchen in Malaysia?
For a wet kitchen with heavy cooking and humidity, many contractors recommend plywood or aluminium carcasses over melamine on particle board, which is more vulnerable to water. Melamine suits dry kitchens and tighter budgets.
